episode_title: Surviving The Hot Seat: Making The Leap From Legal To Strategic Advisor With Chaka Patterson

real_qa.q: What did Chaka Patterson do to establish peer credibility when promoted from deputy general counsel to general counsel at Adtolem?
real_qa.r: Patterson created and headed a COVID task force reporting to the CEO, which freed her from day-to-day COVID management while allowing him to lead a high-powered cross-functional team including business unit heads, the CFO, CHRO, and campus leaders. He held daily 8 a.m. meetings and self-appointed himself as head, which signaled to peers that he was thinking strategically beyond his legal role and breaking out of the deputy perception.
real_qa.requete: How Chaka Patterson became peer to C-suite after GC promotion

real_qa.q: How did Chaka Patterson learn to open a new school campus in Barbados without prior real estate or international experience?
real_qa.r: Patterson applied the same learning approach he used to become treasurer at Exelon: extensive reading, studying, and talking to many people. He negotiated with the prime minister's office and central bank on currency retention during tourist seasons, secured tax exemptions, and handled real estate in a foreign country—demonstrating that a litigator's superpower is knowing how to learn.
real_qa.requete: Chaka Patterson Barbados school opening strategy

real_qa.q: Why did Chaka Patterson move from partner at Jones Day to deputy general counsel at Adtolem despite already having successful litigation experience?
real_qa.r: Patterson sought the deputy GC role at Adtolem because his client and close friend Stephen Beard, who became general counsel, needed someone to manage significant litigation while he handled the GC transition. They agreed that Patterson would be Beard's successor when Beard moved to the business side. The company had just settled an FTC investigation for approximately one hundred million dollars and faced tremendous ongoing litigation.
real_qa.requete: Why Chaka Patterson became deputy general counsel Adtolem

real_qa.q: What is the primary mindset shift required when transitioning from deputy general counsel to general counsel role?
real_qa.r: The shift requires moving from providing pure legal advice to providing strategic advice. As general counsel, C-suite peers want strategic guidance on what to do after receiving legal advice, not the legal advice itself. Patterson notes that legal advice should come from the deputy and subject matter experts, while the GC weighs in on strategy like other executive leadership team members.
real_qa.requete: General counsel legal advice versus strategic advice transition

real_qa.q: What background experiences prepared Chaka Patterson for the general counsel role at a public company?
real_qa.r: Patterson's path included federal judicial clerkships that taught him legal research and writing, partnership at Jenner & Block where he learned rigor and high emotional quotient from mentors like Tony Belukas and Tom Sullivan, government experience as a lawyer in the Illinois Attorney General's office leading his own litigation unit, five years as treasurer and head of investor relations at Exelon, and an MBA from the University of Chicago Booth School during his time as a partner at Jones Day.
real_qa.requete: Chaka Patterson background path to general counsel

guest.bio_context: Chaka Patterson has held roles as a litigator at Jenner & Block, a law firm partner, a government lawyer in the Illinois Attorney General's office, and served as public company treasurer and head of investor relations at Exelon. He was General Counsel of Adtolem Global Education and stepped into the GC role in February 2020, one month before the COVID-19 pandemic. He holds an MBA from the University of Chicago Booth School of Business and is the author of the bestselling book The Hot Seat: Mastering the Public Company General Counsel Role.
